info.name: Kimo Games Admin API
info.description:
The admin panel, `/api/v1/admin`.

Same envelope as the player API — `{ "message": "…", "data": { … } }` on success, `{ "message": "…" }` on error — with one deliberate exception: **Export users to CSV** writes a file, not an envelope.

**Staff accounts are not players.** They live in their own table, so nothing about a player — a wallet, a referral code, a game session — is implied by having one, and a bug in player code can never hand somebody the panel.

**There is no admin sign-up.** No registration, no email verification, no password reset. An account exists because somebody ran this on the server:

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml run --rm app \
  node dist/database/create-admin.js --email=ops@kimogames.online --name="Ops"
```

It prints a password once. Run it again for the same email to reset that password.

**Order to run**

Start with `10 · Admin auth → Log in`. It stores `admin_access_token` and `admin_refresh_token` in collection variables, and every other request here uses them automatically.

**Before you start**

Set `base_url` and the `admin_email` / `admin_password` variables. Requests that act on one row take an id from a collection variable — `tournament_id`, `reward_id`, `player_id`, `puzzle_image_id`, `question_id` — and the create calls fill those in for you as you go.

**Status codes**

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Read or mutation succeeded |
| 201 | Created |
| 400 | A business rule rejected it |
| 401 | Missing, expired or invalid token |
| 403 | A valid token without a staff role |
| 404 | Not found |
| 409 | Conflict — a name, email or entry code already in use |
| 422 | Validation failed (Zod) |
| 429 | Rate limited |

item.name: Admin auth

request.description:
**Public.** The only way into the panel.

**Body**
- `email` — the staff address
- `password` — printed once by `npm run admin:create`

`200` → `{ "message": "Login successful", "data": { "access_token": "…", "refresh_token": "…", "admin": { "id": "…", "name": "Ops", "email": "…", "role": "super_admin", "last_login_at": "…" } } }`

Stores both tokens in collection variables, so nothing below needs copy-paste.

A wrong email and a wrong password cost the same time and read the same — `401 "Incorrect credentials"` — on purpose.

**Errors**
- `401` wrong credentials, or the account is suspended
- `429` more than 10 attempts a minute

**Public.** Rotates the pair. The old refresh token is consumed.

Presenting a refresh token that has already been used revokes the whole family — that is replay detection, not a bug. Log in again.

An account suspended since the token was issued cannot refresh its way back in.

`200` → `{ "data": { "access_token": "…", "refresh_token": "…" } }`

**Errors**
- `401` unknown, expired or replayed token

`200` → `{ "message": "Logged out" }`

The signed-in staff account.

`200` → `{ "data": { "id": "…", "name": "Ops", "email": "…", "role": "super_admin", "last_login_at": "…" } }`

`role` is `support`, `admin` or `super_admin`.

**Errors**
- `401` no token
- `403` a player's token — staff accounts live in their own table

There is no admin sign-up, no email verification and no password reset. An account exists because somebody ran `npm run admin:create` on the server; the same command run again resets its password.

Admin tokens are the same shape as a player's but carry a staff role. Every request in the folders below needs one.

item.name: Admin dashboard

request.description:
Everything on the dashboard in one call.

**Query**
- `range` — `today` (default), `7d` or `30d`. The picker at the top right.

`200` → `{ "data": {
  "range": "today",
  "tiles": { "total_users": { "value": 28756, "change_percent": 12.5 }, "active_users": …, "signups": …, "rounds_played": …, "coins_awarded": …, "revenue_kobo": …, "ad_views": …, "coins_redeemed": …, "tournament_entries": …, "installs": … },
  "coins": { "earned": 1800000, "redeemed": 900000, "in_circulation": 2700000 },
  "daily_active": [ { "day": "2026-08-15", "value": 4200 } ],
  "rounds_by_day": [ { "day": "2026-08-15", "value": 12400 } ],
  "activity": [ … ], "top_players": [ … ], "upcoming_tournaments": [ … ] } }`

`change_percent` is `null` when the previous window was zero — growth from nothing has no percentage worth printing.

Days run on the **Lagos** boundary, the same one missions and daily bonuses use. The line chart is 14 days, the bars 7, both zero-filled so a quiet day is a gap rather than a missing point.

The donut divides everything **ever** earned against everything ever spent, which is a different question from the coin tiles — those only count the window.

response.name: Response

item.description: One call for the whole screen. Every figure is measured against the window immediately before it, which is what the little green percentages compare against.

item.name: Admin users

request.description:
**Query**
- `search` — matches name, username, email and phone
- `status` — `unverified`, `active`, `flagged`, `suspended` or `banned`
- `page`, `limit` — default 1 and 20, max 100

`200` → `{ "data": { "items": [ { "id": "…", "name": "John Doe", "username": "john_d", "email": "john@gmail.com", "phone_number": "+2349037716931", "avatar_url": "…", "coins": 2504, "cash_kobo": 150000, "games_played": 140, "status": "active", "created_at": "…", "last_login_at": "…" } ], "total": 1856, "page": 1, "limit": 20 } }`

Balances come from a join and rounds from a count, so nothing here can drift from the wallet or the sessions themselves.

request.description:
Adds a player on somebody's behalf.

**Body**
- `first_name`, `surname`
- `email` — unique
- `phone_number` — `08031234567` or `+2348031234567`, normalised on the way in
- `username` — 3–20 chars, unique
- `password` — the admin sets it and reads it out

`201` → the created player.

**Verified on the spot and given a wallet.** There is no email to confirm and nobody is emailed — the account is as real as staff say it is. Verification normally creates the wallet, so skipping it means one is created here instead.

**Errors**
- `409` email or username already taken
- `422` a weak password or a malformed phone number

**Not the usual envelope.** This writes a CSV straight to the response — it is a file the browser saves, so there is no `message` wrapper.

**Query** — the same filters as the table:
- `search`, `status`

No paging: the point is the whole list.

`200`, `Content-Type: text/csv`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="kimo-players-2026-08-22.csv"`

Fields holding a comma, a quote or a newline are wrapped so they stay one cell.

In Postman use **Send and Download** to keep the file.

request.description:
Send only what changed. At least one field is required.

**Body**
- `max_coins` — the *Set Amount (Coin)* field, 0–10000
- `maintenance` — `true` closes the game to players
- `randomise_images` — picture puzzle only
- `difficulty` — XOXO only: `simple`, `medium`, `hard`, `very_hard`

Merged into the game's config rather than replacing it, so the timings and the play gate survive an edit.

**`maintenance: true` closes the game**: it disappears from `GET /games` and starting a round returns *"That game is not available"*. Rounds already in flight are unaffected.

**`difficulty` is the lever on what XOXO pays out.** Each setting aims at a share of rounds — player / opponent / draw:

| Setting | Target | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| `simple` | 70 / 20 / 10 | 67 / 19 / 14 |
| `medium` | 40 / 40 / 20 | 40 / 44 / 16 |
| `hard` | 30 / 50 / 20 | 29 / 48 / 23 |
| `very_hard` | 10 / 70 / 20 | 11 / 53 / 36 |

Very Hard cannot reach 70% opponent wins: past a certain strength the extra rounds become draws rather than wins, because a player who blocks cannot be beaten at noughts and crosses. The player's one-in-ten share is the part that governs payouts, and that lands.

No setting is a fixed script — each round draws its own strength from a band, so there is no pattern to read. **A match already in progress keeps the difficulty it started with**, so raising it mid-tournament does not change a match somebody is halfway through.

**Errors**
- `422` empty body, or a difficulty outside the four

`multipart/form-data`. In Postman: Body → form-data → set `file`'s type from Text to File.

**Fields**
- `name` — 2–80 chars, and part of the address, so re-uploading the same name replaces the picture rather than orphaning it
- `file` — JPEG, PNG or WebP, up to **8MB**

Delivered at **exactly 1000×1000**, because the puzzle cuts a 5×5 grid of 200px tiles out of it. A picture of any shape is normalised on the way in.

`201` → `{ "data": { "id": "…", "name": "Market Day", "image_url": "…" } }`

**Errors**
- `400` no file, wrong type, or over 8MB
- `409` that name is already in the library

Removing the **last** picture is refused — the puzzle needs something to deal from.

Removing any other is safe for rounds already in progress: a session holds the tile addresses it started with, and Cloudinary still serves them.

`200` → `{ "message": "Picture removed" }`

**Errors**
- `400` it is the only picture left
- `404` no such picture

request.description:
`multipart/form-data`, **one category per upload**.

**Fields**
- `category` — 2–60 chars, e.g. `Football`
- `file` — CSV, up to 2MB, with exactly this header:

```csv
prompt,option_1,option_2,option_3,option_4,answer
"Which river runs through Ibadan, and how long?",Ogunpa,Niger,Benue,Osun,1
Nigeria gained independence in 1960.,True,False,,,1
```

`answer` counts **from one**, not zero — a spreadsheet full of zero-based indexes is a mistake waiting to happen. Leave `option_3` and `option_4` empty for true/false.

`201` → `{ "data": { "category": "Football", "added": 28, "duplicates": 2, "rejected": [ { "row": 14, "reason": "answer is not one of the options" } ] } }`

**A bad row is reported and skipped, never fatal** — two hundred good questions should not be lost to one typo. Re-runnable: a prompt already in that category is counted as a duplicate rather than doubled, ignoring case.

**Errors**
- `400` no file, or the header is wrong

Entrants who never played are listed with `points: 0` — the board is who entered, not only who scored. Ties break on who got there first.

Ranked in SQL from the scores themselves rather than the Redis board players see, since this is the screen a prize is settled from.

request.description:
The *View List* behind a finished tournament.

`200` → `{ "data": { "items": [ { "username": "hope_a", "email": "hope@example.com", "registered_at": "…", "entry_fee_paid": 500, "points": 1250, "games_scored": 3 } ] } }`

`entry_fee_paid` is what that player actually paid, so a later fee change cannot rewrite history.

Takes a **start and a length**, not two timestamps — nobody thinks in end times.

**Body**
- `name` — 3–120 chars
- `starts_at` — ISO date
- `duration_minutes` — 15 to 20160 (two weeks)
- `registration_opens_at` — optional, defaults to now
- `entry_fee_coins` — 0 for free entry
- `prize_pool_kobo` — kobo, so ₦50,000 is `5000000`
- `attempts_per_game` — 1–20, default 3. Their best qualifying score counts.
- `participant_limit` — `null` for no limit
- `entry_code` — 4–16 letters and numbers, or `null` for an open tournament
- `banner_url` — optional

`201` → the created tournament.

**`entry_code` makes it private**: registration then demands it. Players send it as `{ "entry_code": "hylhra" }` and any case will do. A player's own view says only `entry_code_required: true` — never the code.

**Errors**
- `409` that entry code is already in use
- `422` a start in the past, or a duration outside the range

Send only what changed.

**Moving the start moves the end with it** and keeps the length. Send `duration_minutes` to change the length instead.

`200` → the updated tournament.

**Errors**
- `400` it is already over
- `409` the entry code is taken
- `404` no such tournament

Sets the status to `cancelled`. **It never deletes.** Entries, scores and the fees people paid are the record of what happened, and a tournament nobody entered is still the one that was advertised.

`200` → `{ "message": "Tournament cancelled" }`

**Errors**
- `400` it has already finished
- `404` no such tournament

Puts a cancelled one back, as `upcoming` or `live` depending on its own clock.

`200` → the restored tournament.

**Errors**
- `400` it was not cancelled, or its window has already passed

request.description:
Both halves of the wallet screen in one call.

**Query**
- `range` — `today` (default), `7d`, `30d`

`200` → `{ "data": { "range": "today", "cash": { … }, "coins": { … }, "charts": { … }, "recent": { … } } }`

**Cash:** `total_customer_funds`, `funds_added`, `funds_spent`, `reversals`, `active_wallets`, `pending_deposits`, `failed_payments`, plus `all_time`. `funds_withdrawn`, `pending_withdrawals` and `refunds` are `null`.

**Coins:** `coins_in_circulation`, `bonus_in_circulation`, `coins_earned`, `coins_spent`, `coins_reversed`, `coins_expired`, `pending_redemptions`, `rewards_claimed`, `by_source`, `by_sink`, `top_games`. `failed_transactions` is `null`.

**`bonus_in_circulation` is a portion of `coins_in_circulation`, not a separate pot.** `coins_expired` counts bonus coins that reached the end of their week without being spent.

**Charts:** `cash_balance_trend` is the balance at the end of each of the last 14 days, worked back from today's total by undoing every movement since — balances are not stored per day, and reconstructing them this way cannot drift from the ledger.

**Recent:** `cash_transactions`, `coin_transactions` and `pending_redemptions`, each with the player's username.

request.description:
The six summary cards. No `range` — every figure is all-time, which is what a report means here.

`200` → `{ "data": { "items": [
  { "report": "payments", "title": "Payment Report", "headline": "Total Volume", "value": 24850000, "format": "kobo" },
  { "report": "wallet", "headline": "Total Coins Earned", "value": 18450250, "format": "coins" },
  { "report": "users", … }, { "report": "games", … },
  { "report": "tournaments", … }, { "report": "revenue", … } ] } }`

`format` says how to render `value` — `kobo` divides by 100 and prefixes ₦, `coins` and `count` print as they are, `text` is already a string (the top game's name).

Each card's *View Report* downloads the PDF below.

request.description:
The card's *View Report*, as a branded PDF.

`report` is `payments`, `wallet`, `users`, `games`, `tournaments` or `revenue`.

Returns `application/pdf` with `Content-Disposition: attachment`, so **use Send and Download** — this one does not answer with the usual envelope, because a PDF is a file the browser saves.

All-time figures, the platform logo, and the date it was generated.

**Errors**
- `422` `report` is not one of the six

Moves a player's balance by hand.

**Super admin only.** A `support` or `admin` token gets `403`.

**Body**
- `user_id`
- `currency` — `coin` or `cash`
- `amount` — negative takes it away. Zero is refused.
- `reason` — 4–300 characters, and it is stored

`200` → `{ "message": "Balance adjusted", "data": { "user_id": "…", "currency": "coin", "balance_before": 5000, "balance_after": 5500 } }`

**Every call writes an audit row** with the actor, the amount, the balance before and after, and the reason. That is required of anything that moves money by hand — an adjustment without those is indistinguishable from a bug.

**A credit here is gameplay coins, never bonus.** A correction a player is owed should still be there next week rather than expiring on Sunday.

**Errors**
- `400` the player would go below zero
- `403` not a super admin
- `422` zero amount, or a reason under four characters

item.description:
The Payments, Wallet and Reports screens. Every figure is measured against the window immediately before it, and days run on the Lagos boundary.

**A `null` figure means we do not hold that data**, not zero. Withdrawals and refunds are not part of this product, and a coin movement either commits or does not, so there is no failed-coin count. Show those as N/A rather than 0 — zero reads as "none today" when the truth is "we do not do this".
